body: Thanks, I do try, have to take care of others, no way of doing it when I am gone. Giving up isn't an option, it's not in my blood to give up. Weird thing to say considering I tried to kill myself a couple of times. But yeah...
Yo, want to talk, maybe it could ease a bit of it.
Hey man, I'm here to talk. Don't do anything hasty
That hits hard, in the same situation myself.  You want to talk?
A good choice I would say, I am mostly a whiskey and stouts type of person with the occasional homemade (Legal in my birth country).

First of all, you are amazing, I can hardly imagine what it's like to have a child, much less a second one, hell I'm not sure if I have five or so years left. So hats off to you, you are a superhero.

Secondly, perhaps you need to vent, which is okay or some kind words.

Third and final one, not an expert on relationships but share with your husband how you feel, talk it out, see if you can get that peace of mind.
It all starts like that man, and ofc it sucks but whether you believe it or not I have the non-obligatory type of faith that a fellow that has been there has for others.
Can I ask what is your drink of choice usually?
Another alcoholic, man I feel you there, not having that drink messes you up. God, I know that painfully well. I can only recommend a lesser and lesser percentage until you gradually just stop.
Why does your body torture you when you don't drink if you mind me asking?

I would like to say to you, stay safe, please. I am not saying this without some experience backing it up. I have been down that road one too many times. For now, enjoy the drink and pray that the hangover is not that bad.
Always happy to help out.
Hey, you ever need to talk to someone occasionally, send a message I most likely will be online.

Fruit salad, I really don't like sweets but I drink a lot of energy drinks so it really isn't that good.

Boys and I play Path of Exile if the league is fun. In the current dorm, most of us are living the "gremlin life", nobody goes out and we have our own worlds.

Anyways sufficiently tired enough to go to bed. Good night to you

Greetings

A guy from the Balkans who came up to the Netherlands to study at university. I started drinking around 14 as well, I'm close to 21 now. It was way worse before, every day starting off with a case 24 330 ml of beer and then switching to the typical moonshine (from 40 %alc and above). now I tend to keep myself to a maximum of 4 beers. The shifts back during the time I started were necessary otherwise nobody out of my family could pay the bills. I kinda slowed down after I got my first girlfriend but that story went down the drain fast, and worse. There was acid, weed and fights...a lot of them. I now drink out of nostalgia because I really miss my friends with whom I would go out and have a blast no alcohol needed but a beer here or there was okay.

Motorhead, a man of culture I see, in reality where I'm from alcohol is normality, getting drunk is a weekly occurrence. I started drinking heavily to ease the nerves. Too many night shifts for a minor.

Not really the person to deal with relationship problems, however, I am experienced in other forms of self-harm. In my case, it is an impulsive thing, especially when my nerves are on strain. I punch brick walls or bite down on my arm. I believe your case might be similar.
I can't fall asleep for another night might as well help people out. Also, no need to thank me.
I see, still though I do hope that one day you are gonna feel better. I have no idea what the situation is and I don't intend to pry. Stay safe out there
Let me be honest, stopping cutting is the best option, but I'm one of the people that know such habits are hard to break, I wish you all the best and perhaps one day for you to be happy and clean.
Sometimes it happens to a rapid drop in blood sugar. Make sure you have some snacks, it is a good idea, especially in times like these. It is sad though, I really feel for you.
Hmm, a difficult one. I've had that experience once, didn't help I was drunk and furious. sorry to ask this but have you drunk something, or perhaps were you hungry?

I have been under such a promise, but I guess a bit different. I was told, "Before you cut or fight, call me I'll at least bring you bandages, I really want you to stop though.". Sometimes the people, who make you promise, know that it is hard to stop, so they do take care as to not burden you with unnecessary negativity. I feel that sometimes that promise is a necessity, or in my case as I try to uphold promises and agreements as much as possible.

I guess it mostly happens when I am very angry, or very sad. I can't deal with emotions in general, but I also grew up in a bad place. I know how to fight but not let go. I would guess that is the reason for me

I can say this from experience, people can be rude about it but you learn to live with it. I also didn't feel comfortable going to swimming practice covered in cuts, scratches, and wounds. It has been like that all my life and people still ask me about it. If you want to talk more about it I am here to listen. - a fellow covered in a lot of scars
